Left off the $\sin 31^{\circ}$ factor, computing just $7/\sin 84^{\circ}$.
Divided the wrong way, computing $5\sin 63^{\circ}/\sin 27^{\circ}$ instead of $5\sin 27^{\circ}/\sin 63^{\circ}$.
Treated the angles as plain numbers, computing $5\times27/63$.
Put the unknown over $\sin 65^{\circ}$ instead of over its own opposite angle $\sin 47^{\circ}$.
Found the side opposite the third angle $68^{\circ}$ instead of the one opposite $47^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
The $16$ cm side is opposite the $65^{\circ}$ angle, and $x$ is opposite the $47^{\circ}$ angle.
$\dfrac{x}{\sin 47^{\circ}}=\dfrac{16}{\sin 65^{\circ}}$
$x=\dfrac{16\sin 47^{\circ}}{\sin 65^{\circ}}$
$\approx 12.9\text{ cm}$

questions.solution_text:
The $13$ m side is opposite the $48^{\circ}$ angle, and $x$ is opposite the $55^{\circ}$ angle.
$\dfrac{x}{\sin 55^{\circ}}=\dfrac{13}{\sin 48^{\circ}}$
$x=\dfrac{13\sin 55^{\circ}}{\sin 48^{\circ}}$
$\approx 14.3\text{ m}$

options.why: Divided the wrong way, putting the unknown over $\sin 66^{\circ}$ instead of the $30$ cm side.
Paired the $30$ cm base with $61^{\circ}$ instead of finding the top angle $66^{\circ}$ opposite it.

questions.solution_text:
The $30$ cm side is opposite the unmarked top angle, so find it first.
$180^{\circ}-53^{\circ}-61^{\circ}=66^{\circ}$
$\dfrac{x}{\sin 53^{\circ}}=\dfrac{30}{\sin 66^{\circ}}$
$x=\dfrac{30\sin 53^{\circ}}{\sin 66^{\circ}}$
$\approx 26.2\text{ cm}$

options.why: Found $MT$, the distance opposite $71^{\circ}$, instead of $NT$.
Paired the $120$ m side with $71^{\circ}$ instead of the angle opposite it, $55^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$NT$ is opposite $\angle M$. The $120$ m side ($MN$) is opposite $\angle T$, so find $\angle T$ first.
$\angle T=180^{\circ}-54^{\circ}-71^{\circ}=55^{\circ}$
$\dfrac{NT}{\sin 54^{\circ}}=\dfrac{120}{\sin 55^{\circ}}$
$NT=\dfrac{120\sin 54^{\circ}}{\sin 55^{\circ}}$
$\approx 118.5\text{ m}$

options.why: Found $DF$, the leg opposite $52^{\circ}$, instead of $EF$.
Paired the $3.5$ km leg with $52^{\circ}$ instead of the angle opposite it, $67^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$EF$ is opposite $\angle D$. The $3.5$ km leg ($DE$) is opposite $\angle F$, so find $\angle F$ first.
$\angle F=180^{\circ}-61^{\circ}-52^{\circ}=67^{\circ}$
$\dfrac{EF}{\sin 61^{\circ}}=\dfrac{3.5}{\sin 67^{\circ}}$
$EF=\dfrac{3.5\sin 61^{\circ}}{\sin 67^{\circ}}$
$\approx 3.33\text{ km}$

options.why: Added only the two computed sides and left out the given side $GH$.
Divided by the wrong angle's sine when finding each side, using $45^{\circ}$ and $63^{\circ}$ rather than the opposite angle $72^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$GH$ is opposite $\angle K$, so find $\angle K$ first.
$\angle K=180^{\circ}-45^{\circ}-63^{\circ}=72^{\circ}$
$GK$ is opposite $\angle H$:
$GK=\dfrac{18\sin 63^{\circ}}{\sin 72^{\circ}}$
$\approx 16.86\text{ m}$
$HK$ is opposite $\angle G$:
$HK=\dfrac{18\sin 45^{\circ}}{\sin 72^{\circ}}$
$\approx 13.38\text{ m}$
$18+16.86+13.38\approx 48.2\text{ m}$
